label: illustrative: invented product and facts, written for testing the skill (A3 and A4); not a real design
outcome: Fewer panic attacks per week at 12 weeks
population: Adults with panic disorder in outpatient care, smartphone owners

links.text: Users complete interoceptive exposure exercises at least 3 times a week
Exposure is expected to reduce fear of bodily sensations (psychological capability and automatic motivation)
Reduced fear is expected to reduce panic attack frequency

adaptive.rule: Next level if distress at end is below start

assumptions.text: Users will complete exposure despite discomfort
assumptions.signal: Completion below the person's milestone by week 4

assumptions.text: Exposure reduces fear of bodily sensations in app delivery

users_and_money.users: Adults with panic disorder, as the person states
users_and_money.payment: Monthly subscription after a 7-day free trial; cancellation by emailing support

mechanics.name: Daily streak counter
mechanics.usage_measure: Consecutive days with an exposure exercise logged

mechanics.name: Exposure reminder, 3 per week
mechanics.usage_measure: Reminders opened; exercises started within 1 hour
mechanics.justification: Matches the exposure schedule in the team's treatment manual

flags.pattern: reminder repeats every hour until opened (nagging)

mechanics.name: Streak-save reminder at 23:00
mechanics.health_risk: late-night prompts; decreased sleep quality is a pattern named in a precedent's risk table (SE16)

mechanics.name: Exit screen: 'Quitting now means panic wins. Are you sure?'

flags.pattern: confirmshaming could be an aggressive practice (UCPD guidance)

mechanics.name: Cancellation by email to support only

flags.pattern: no simple mechanism to stop recurring charges

hazards.text: An exposure exercise triggers a severe panic attack and the user has no route to help
hazards.indicator: Complaints or support messages reporting panic during an exercise

hazards.text: A user stops prescribed medication believing the app replaces it
hazards.mitigation: Adjunct statement in onboarding and settings (the person's)
